title: Struct layout
description: Offsets, padding awareness, and little-endian fields
theory:
### Records as ordered layout

A **struct** is a block of fields at fixed offsets. NASM does not know about Rust or C
layouts automatically; you either equate offsets (`struc`/`istruc` support in NASM) or
document them and address fields as **`base + displacement`**.

Padding appears when types naturally align to machine boundaries—mirror what **`clang`**
would emit if you need to share a struct with C **`extern`** functions.

### Example record in `.data`

```nasm
struc Point
    .x: resd 1
    .y: resd 1
endstruc

section .data
    origin: istruc Point
        at Point.x, dd 2
        at Point.y, dd 3
    iend
```

### Loading members

Use appropriately sized moves: **`dword`** for 32-bit fields, **`qword`** for pointers.
Sign-extend or zero-extend when promoting narrower fields to **`rax`** for arithmetic,
matching how compilers prepare values before AMD64 operations.

exercises.title: Field offset
exercises.description: In `.data`, define bytes: tag `'x'` then value `'7'` (two contiguous bytes). Print the **second** byte only (`7`, no newline), then exit 0.
exercises.starter_code:
global _start
section .data
rec:
    db 'x'
    db '7'
section .text
_start:
    ; rsi points to second byte
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall
exercises.solution:
global _start
section .data
rec:
    db 'x'
    db '7'
section .text
_start:
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    lea rsi, [rel rec+1]
    mov rdx, 1
    syscall
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall

exercises.title: Little-endian dword
exercises.description: Place a **4-byte** little-endian dword with value `3` at label `n` (`dd 3`). Print the character `'3'` (one byte) by loading the **least-significant** byte of `n` and writing it—**not** by embedding another `'3'` literal elsewhere.
exercises.starter_code:
global _start
section .data
n: dd 3
section .text
_start:
    ; movzx from first byte of n, add '0', write one digit
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall
hints: `movzx eax, byte [rel n]` gives `3` for `dd 3` on little-endian
exercises.solution:
global _start
section .bss
    digit: resb 1
section .data
n: dd 3
section .text
_start:
    movzx eax, byte [rel n]
    add eax, '0'
    mov [rel digit], al
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    lea rsi, [rel digit]
    mov rdx, 1
    syscall
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall

exercises.title: Packed pair
exercises.description: Two consecutive 16-bit words: first is `0`, second has numeric value `0x32` (so the **low byte** is ASCII `'2'`). Print that single low byte (`'2'`, no newline), then exit 0.
exercises.starter_code:
global _start
section .data
pair:
    dw 0
    dw 0x32
section .text
_start:
    ; second word starts at pair+2
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall
exercises.solution:
global _start
section .data
pair:
    dw 0
    dw 0x32
section .text
_start:
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    lea rsi, [rel pair+2]
    mov rdx, 1
    syscall
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall

exercises.title: Three-byte record
exercises.description: Contiguous bytes `db 'f','u','n'` at label `tri`. Print the **middle** byte `u` (no newline) using offset `1`, then exit 0.
exercises.starter_code:
global _start
section .data
tri:
    db 'f','u','n'
section .text
_start:
    ; lea rsi, [rel tri+1]; write 1 byte
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall
exercises.solution:
global _start
section .data
tri:
    db 'f', 'u', 'n'
section .text
_start:
    mov rax, 1
    mov rdi, 1
    lea rsi, [rel tri+1]
    mov rdx, 1
    syscall
    mov rax, 60
    xor rdi, rdi
    syscall
